about: One entry per app. The chat named here is the only chat that works on that app. A chat reads its own entry before it starts and writes it back when it stops. status: needs = waiting on Jerry; review = finished work to look at; open = work outstanding; clear = nothing waiting; no-chat = no chat owns this app yet. repo: the GitHub repo an app lives in when it is not this one; blank means daraja-apps.

apps.next: Round live. Jerry sent Emmanuel Koki and Veronicah Kimani their team messages on 5 Nov, so the seven days close on 12 Nov — or sooner per app, once two testers pass it on its current version. Two teams, 14 and 13 people, in testers/teams.md; the roster of 27 invited is kenya/roster.md. PAY IS UNDECIDED: Jerry paid the October round himself and has not said whether this one is paid, and neither message mentioned it — so do not quote a figure to anyone. Six apps start the round needing passes: the Daraja front door and Duka (never tested by anyone), Receipt Maker, and Rafiki, Ahead of It and In My Own Words on their 4 Nov versions. Six finds by Fredrick Nganga and Brian Maina Kamau are still unconfirmed and want Jerry's word when the round closes. SINCE 6 NOV, EIGHT MORE APPS HAVE A NEW VERSION and so start from zero passes on it: Business Manager v1.6 and its Kenya edition v1.5, Our Table v1.19, Every Day v1.14, Message Assistant v1.10, Serve Board v1.10, Shoebox Counter v1.18 (all gained a WhatsApp button beside their text button) and Who's Coming v1.18 (a read-only link to the answers). Their test scripts gained steps for the new buttons, so the Ready to Sell page will show them as 'almost' rather than 'ready' until two testers pass each one again — there are six days left to do that. THE LIST WAS REORDERED THE SAME DAY so those apps lead it, and Shoebox Counter and Our Table came out of Group 3 at Jerry's word, making the live list 22 apps: OCC collection week is mid-November, so the app with the nearest real-world date had been the one app no tester could reach. A tester opening the list now sees Our Table, One Thing, Advent Together, Shoebox Counter, then the rest. JERRY SENT EMMANUEL AND VERONICAH A FRESH WHATSAPP MESSAGE ON 6 NOV naming all seven changed apps and asking for Shoebox Counter first. That matters for judging the round: if reports are still at zero after this, it is zero after a direct nudge, which is a stronger signal than the silence of 5 Nov. LATER ON 6 NOV THE DIAGNOSIS CHANGED. On 5 Nov Jerry messaged only the two LEADS, not the 27, the plan being that each lead passes it to their own team. There is no evidence Veronicah ever relayed hers: Faith Wangari, Frank Ndung'u and Ruth Waitherero Kiarie are on her roster, are free of Zuri entirely, covered 28, 28 and 25 apps in October, and have filed nothing. The likeliest cause is that nobody told them the round started, not that they are unwilling. So on 6 Nov Jerry sent TWO more messages, in this order: one to Veronicah asking whether her team got the word and telling her the next one was coming, then one to Faith, Frank and Ruth as a REMINDER rather than an invitation, with her copied. Neither mentioned pay. That is the test: if reports now come from those three, the fault was the relay, and every future round needs the leads' messages confirmed as passed on rather than assumed. If it is still zero after a direct nudge to the three strongest testers who have no other claim on them, the cause is something else and worth finding before the next round. Nothing is waiting on Jerry until reports come in. A DAILY WATCH NOW EXISTS, created 7 Nov at Jerry's word ("The two big groups are starting now so you should be watching them somehow"): "Daraja round — did anybody test today?" (trig_01GNw7MRvvQT66PEJf4CwnpM), 20:10 Nairobi daily, firing into this chat. It exports the sheet, re-runs the morning report and says who tested and which apps moved. If nothing came in it says so in ONE line and stops — Jerry already knows the round is at zero and a daily restatement is noise. This closes the gap named above: Zuri had a morning breakage check and an evening watch while Daraja had nobody chasing it, which is how ten days of silence went unnoticed. CHECKED 7 NOV 15:00 UTC against a fresh export: the newest report anywhere in the sheet is still 2026-10-28T12:37, and all thirteen apps needing passes have zero on their current version — so the 6 Nov direct reminder to Faith, Frank and Ruth produced nothing either, which rules out the relay as the cause. PAY IS RECORDED THREE DIFFERENT WAYS AND THEY DO NOT AGREE — found 7 Nov, still Jerry's to settle: kenya/pay.md says 250 KES per completed app-test "starts with the next round"; this entry says pay is undecided for this round; the Zuri evening watch's own prompt says pay is settled and he is done paying. Nobody can tell a tester anything about pay until he says which is true. THE LEADS' PAY PAGE IS LIVE from 7 Nov — kenya/pay/, one link each: ?lead=emmanuel, ?lead=veronicah, and no lead for both (Jerry's view). Earned is counted nightly by tools/payroll/payroll.py off the same sheet; paid is tapped by the lead and stored in the testers' mailbox as a post with kind "paid", so nothing needed a key or a redeploy. ONE GAP, NOT YET CLOSED: nothing commits kenya/payroll.json on a schedule, so the page shows whatever was last committed and will go stale exactly as the Kenya Test Tally did. The fix is one step inside the evening watch (trig_01GNw7MRvvQT66PEJf4CwnpM), which already exports the sheet and runs refresh.sh: compare the fresh payroll.json with the repo's, ignoring `updated`, and commit just that file when a number has moved. CLOSED on 7 Nov once Jerry allowed it: the watch now compares the fresh payroll.json against the repo's, ignoring `updated`, and commits just that one file to main when a number has moved. It is the only thing in that job that writes to main, and it never edits a figure by hand — if payroll.py fails it says so and leaves the committed file alone. ALSO FOUND, Jerry's to settle: seven people have filed 108 reports between them and are on NEITHER team, so no lead pays them — Shamsuddin Jamal Mukira (31), Josphat Thuo (28), Nessy Mukami (21), Thao mita (20), Francis Koikai (6), Clinton Mburu (1), Jacqueline Nkirote Muriithi (1). Shamsuddin covered 28 apps in October, more than anyone on Veronicah's roster but Faith.

apps.name: Daraja Compass
apps.next: WAITING ON JERRY: one paste. He chose on 7 Nov to have the Store Manager chat close the last gap in the Compass videos, so the step is to paste the change into https://claude.ai/code/session_01SneDTZZK3LM6dXHfqB8Jeg — that chat owns shop/apps_data.js and a message from another Claude session is not his authority, so it has to come from him. WHAT IS LEFT TO FIX: setPlace('ke') only runs on lines that carry js, and two opening lines are plain strings. In the 2-minute overview — the video on the store card — the “Where are you?” card therefore covers the first two lines, about 20 seconds, while the narration says what Compass is. The first-timer video has it on its first line. The training video is clean. THE CHANGE, TESTED BY THIS CHAT ON 7 NOV: give each of those two opening lines the same js the other 36 lines carry, try{if(typeof place==='function'&&!place())setPlace('ke');}catch(e){} — the lines being “Welcome. This short video explains Daraja Compass…” and “This is Daraja Compass. It is free…”. Applied locally and watched: the card is on screen at 5, 10, 15 and 20 seconds before, and gone from the first sample onwards after, with the screens following the words all through. Then reverted, because the catalogue is not this chat's file to commit. HOW IT WAS WATCHED, SINCE THE USUAL CHECK CANNOT RUN HERE: shop/checkvideos.js loads the app from jerrywins1.github.io, which a cloud container cannot reach, so it reports 0 of 3 for that reason alone. Serving the repo on localhost and overriding BASE in shop/apps_data.js is what works. AND A BLIND SPOT WORTH KNOWING: checkvideos.js passes these videos as they stand, because on a line with no js and no point it tests only for a password box and a blank page — a country card is neither. Same shape as the HQ videos passing while showing their password gate. STILL OPEN AFTERWARDS: the videos pick Kenya for every viewer, which wants revisiting if Compass gets a real US audience; and render() bailing out on needPlace() is a wall for anything driving the app from outside, so curing it there rather than line by line would stop it coming back.
